correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary Boolean algebra, x△y≤y whenever x≤y, so the asserted quasi-law implies f(x)≤f(y). Taking u=x∨y, u△x≤y and monotonicity imply f(u)≤f(x)∨f(y); the reverse inequality is monotonicity. Conversely x=p∨r,y=q∨r with p=x∧¬y,q=y∧¬x,r=x∧y and the lattice identity (a∨c)△(b∨c)≤a∨b yield f(x)△f(y)≤f(x△y)≤f(z). No normality or nontriviality assumption. For each of n labelled output atoms, a join-preserving {0,1}-valued coordinate map is either identically one or is uniquely determined by n singleton bits, hence (2^n+1)^n. Independently enumerated all n=1,2 unary operators: respectively 3/4 and 25/256 satisfy both. The published Example 2.2 f({1,3})={1,2,3} while f({1})={1}, f({3})={3} violates the quasi-law with x={1,3},y={1},z={3}.

originality.rationale: The actual 2026 Gyenis–Molnár–Öztürk primary article asserts the quasi-law to be strictly weaker than additivity and asserts its nonadditive example satisfies it. The independently proved equivalence and explicit violating triple refute those two particular assertions; previous general CEP results do not imply the converse equivalence. Earlier implicit Boolean lattice identities and subsequent versions of the manuscript are residual risks, not grounds to dismiss this demonstrated direct correction.
